Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.
recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Name: Clive de Carle

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Clive's case for proteolytic enzymes", "body": "Clive de Carle calls proteolytic enzymes perhaps the single most important supplement, and explains his reasoning through small children who fall over and bounce back within minutes. In his view an injury can be repaired either with healthy tissue or with scar tissue, and he says our own enzyme production falls noticeably from our thirties, tipping older bodies toward scarring. He sorts most chronic illness into inflammatory 'itis' conditions and scarring 'osis' conditions, and recounts how Japanese scientists studying silkworms, whose moths dissolve a rock hard cocoon in seconds, found the bacteria behind the enzyme he now offers as Prozymes."}, {"title": "Vitamin K2 and the lost Activator X", "body": "Clive traces vitamin K2 to the diets of our ancestors, who mostly ate products from animals grazing fresh spring pasture. He recounts how the dentist Weston Price travelled the world studying teeth, found people on traditional diets largely free of cavities until western food arrived, and named a missing 'Activator X' that he made from spring butter and cod liver oil. For vegans Clive points to natto, the slimy fermented Japanese soybean, and he argues K2 moves calcium out of arteries and back into bones. He adds that truly healthy cows eat wildflowers, herbs and tree leaves, not just grass."}, {"title": "Growing your own health at home", "body": "Answering a listener question, Clive shares low effort ways to grow food at home: laying sprouting potatoes on cardboard under a thick layer of straw so their roots break up hard lawn, stacking straw, soil and potatoes inside a chicken wire barrel for vertical harvests, and replanting celery bases and lettuce ends. He suggests stretching probiotic capsules by culturing them in yogurt, milk or mashed banana, and praises fulvic minerals for energizing plants and people alike. Chance notes that freshly picked food likely carries more nutrition, while Clive argues hydroponic lettuce may never have seen soil and calls NPK fertilizer a leftover of First World War munitions."}, {"title": "Teeth, dentists and medical mercury", "body": "Picking up on Weston Price, Chance asks what people get wrong about dental health. Clive describes a dentist he interviewed who gave up practice to review x-rays and treatment plans for patients around the world, telling them when they are being overcharged or offered a poor filling material, and Chance recalls a childhood dentist whose scary upsell sent his family back to their trusted family dentist. Chance then links his reading on alchemy and resonance architecture to mercury amalgam fillings, and Clive recalls doctors once using mercury against syphilis, glowing mercury buoys at sea, and thimerosal in eye drops from his contact lens days."}, {"title": "Spring water, filters and structured water", "body": "Asked to cut through the debate over alkaline, kangen, distilled and structured water, Clive names spring water bubbling up from clean mountain sources as the best. At home he asked his supplier whether recycled sewage came out of his taps, then chose reverse osmosis over a noisy distiller, and he brings filtered water back to life with fulvic minerals, a pinch of sea salt or a spin, wondering whether distilled water might leach minerals. Chance argues that water is structured by sound, asks what a humming refrigerator does to our food, and describes playing solfeggio tones in his shower, pointing to Masaru Emoto's water experiments."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Clive De Carle returns to InnerVerse to share his nutritional knowledge about the myriad of methods to help our meat-suits mend from any and all maladies, using the building blocks of nature found in natural, food-based medicines. We discuss growing your own "garden-variety" supplements, repairing damage with proteolytic enzymes, "Factor X" and Vitamin K2, healing our teeth, medical mercury, and water strategies.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: In the Plus+ Extension we talk about Clive's experience with mitigating diabetes, the connection between selenium, nutrition and willpower, the innate intelligence of the body, MSM Sulpher, fixing damaged lungs, varieties of Vitamin C, neutralizing toxic tap water with Vitamin C and Borax, wearable laser-therapy devices, and much more!
